findings.obs_text: In Ecc 3:18 heart (H3820A) stands two words before with regard to: the Preacher speaks in his heart about the children of man.
findings.grounds: I said in my heart with regard to the children of man

older.finding: Qohelet's heart reasons to the shared breath, then leaves the spirit's destination open (Ecc 3:18–21). This is the fullest statement that the breath does not mark man off from beast (§1.1). It is also the place where the difference is left unknown rather than denied.
older.reason: it states how heart works in a person; the heart collection owns it

older.finding:
What the heart says is mostly a verdict: about God's seeing, about self, about the future. Kinds seen:
• denial that God sees (Ps 10:11, 13; Zep 1:12; Isa 47:10)
• self-exaltation (Isa 14:13; 47:8; Zep 2:15; Obd 3; Eze 28:2)
• self-credit (Deu 8:17; 9:4)
• fear (Deu 7:17; 1Sa 27:1)
• enquiry (Ecc 1:16; 2:1, 15; 3:17–18; Deu 18:21; Jer 13:22)
• denial of God (Ps 14:1; 53:1)
older.reason: it states how heart works in a person; the heart collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Lam 4:16 honor (H6440N) stands three words after regard, in the parallel lines: the Lord regards them no more and no honor is shown to the priests.
findings.grounds: no honor was shown to the priests

findings.obs_text: In 1Ti 6:1 worthy and honor (G0514, G5092) stand three and five words after regard as what masters are counted: worthy of all honor. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through esteem, a synonym; the verse joins regard and honor.
In Judg 15:3 innocent (H5352) stands directly before in regard to: Samson declares himself innocent toward the Philistines.
findings.grounds: I shall be innocent in regard to the Philistines

findings.obs_text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 blameless (H8535), with integrity (H8538) in Job 2:3, describes the one considered.
In Job 9:21 blameless (H8535) opens the verse, two words before regard: Job, blameless, does not regard himself.
findings.grounds: I am blameless; I regard not myself

findings.obs_text: In Psa 44:22 and Rom 8:36 killed (H2026, G2289) stands three words before regarded, in the parallel line: they are killed all day and counted as sheep for slaughter.
findings.grounds: we are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered

findings.obs_text: In Ecc 12:9 knowledge (H1847) stands directly before weighing: the Preacher taught knowledge, weighing proverbs.

In Mar 10:42 and Act 28:22 know (G6063, G1110) stands near the counting or the link: you know who are considered rulers; we know the sect is spoken against. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through see, a synonym.
findings.grounds: You know that those who are considered rulers

findings.obs_text: In Exo 5:9 work and labor (H5656I, H6213A) stand before regard: heavier work is laid on the men so that they pay no regard to lying words.
findings.grounds: Let heavier work be laid on the men

findings.obs_text: In Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12 works and work (H6468, H4639G, with H0413 at the same places) stand after regard as what is not regarded: the works of the Lord.
findings.grounds: the works of the Lord or the work of his hands

findings.obs_text: In Ecc 2:11 toil (H5999) stands four words after considered as what is considered: the toil the Preacher spent.
findings.grounds: the toil I had expended in doing it

findings.obs_text: In Lam 4:2 work (H4639G) stands three words after regarded, in what the sons are counted as: the work of a potter's hands.
In Zep 1:11 wail (H3213) opens the verse, eight words before weigh: the call to wail is over those who weigh out silver, who are cut off.
findings.grounds: Wail, O inhabitants of the Mortar

findings.obs_text: In 2Ch 6:19 cry (H7440) stands ten words after regard, in what God is asked to regard: the cry and the prayer of his servant.
findings.grounds: listening to the cry and to the prayer
